text:
sam_sales: Hey team — Maria (customer) just asked if we can route model inference traffic from their app VPC into a shared-services VPC that runs a central connector/proxy. They want strict segmentation between teams, minimal security changes on their side, and predictable egress costs. Any recommended patterns?

ian_netops: Two sensible patterns:
1) Shared-services VPC with Interface VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints) per service. Pros: no cross-account routing rules, keeps customer IPs private to AWS backbone. Cons: per-endpoint ENI and cost.
2) Service VPC peering + transit/routing through a central NAT/egress stack. Pros: simpler if lots of services; Cons: source IP preservation is hard without proxy/protocol helpers and controlling route tables gets messy.

julia_se: For our connector, we typically recommend either PrivateLink or a TLS-terminating proxy cluster in shared-services that accepts mutual TLS from customers. If they need source IP for auditing, use a TCP load balancer with PROXY protocol + our connector set to parse PROXY headers.

alex_sec: Security checklist items I care about:
- Only allow 443 inbound to the proxy from customer CIDRs.
- Strict SGs: e.g., sg-conn-ingress: allow tcp 443 from 10.10.0.0/16 (customer app range)
- Egress rules limited to Redwood control plane / model-serving IPs (we give a stable set or FQDN allowlist).
- Client cert mTLS optional; if enabled, cert rotation ops needed.

sam_sales: Maria — do you control the app VPC and can you add SG rules / interface endpoints?

maria_cust: We control the app VPC but want the least config on our side. Prefer to add just one outbound SG rule. Also curious about cost — is there a clear delta between interface endpoints vs NAT egress?

ian_netops: Quick cost notes:
- Interface endpoints: hourly + per-GB data processing by AWS. Cost scales with number of endpoints and traffic.
- NAT/egress via IGW + NAT Gateway: simpler but causes cross-account routing complexity; NAT GW has per-hour + per-GB egress.
- If traffic is steady and high throughput, a dedicated proxy in shared infra on dedicated capacity (our Dedicated offering) can be more cost-predictable.

julia_se: Example minimal SG snippet customers often copy:```
# Allow outbound from app hosts to connector
SecurityGroup: AppOutbound
- Type: Custom TCP
  PortRange: 443
  Source: 10.10.0.0/16
```
And connector SG:```
# Connector inbound
SecurityGroup: ConnectorInbound
- Type: HTTPS
  PortRange: 443
  Source: sg-app-outbound (reference)
```

alex_sec: Also add an egress allowlist for auditing:```
# Connector egress to model-serving endpoints
- Destination: 54.23.11.77/32  # example model node
- Port: 443
```
We can provide the final list during contract.

sam_sales: One gotcha: if you use peering, VPC peering does not support security group referencing across accounts without special role setup; interface endpoints avoid that.

maria_cust: Can we get a short diagram and a list of exact ports/ips to give to our network team? Also timeline — POC next week.

julia_se: I'll sketch a 1-page diagram: two options (1) PrivateLink -> our connector ALB -> connector cluster; (2) Peering -> central proxy NAT -> connector. I'll include SGs, example route-table changes, and a minimal ports/IP list.

ian_netops: For POC, recommend PrivateLink with a single interface endpoint from their VPC to reduce routing churn. That keeps POC scoped and we can measure egress.

deploy-bot: Reminder: we have a reserved port allocation for connector clusters. Opened ticket INF-7629 to provision a canary connector in shared-services for this POC.

sam_sales: Action items:
- julia_se: post diagram + SG & RT snippets (today)
- ian_netops: estimate per-GB costs for endpoint vs NAT for expected POC traffic (~1TB) (today)
- alex_sec: provide minimal security questionnaire answers re: mTLS, logging (EoD)
- maria_cust: confirm whether you can add one SG outbound and whether you want mTLS on day 1

maria_cust: Confirmed — we can add 1 SG outbound. We'll skip mTLS for initial POC; will enable after perf/security signoff. Thanks! :thumbsup:
